fixes.explanation: Paul says the opposite here. He writes, "We know that an idol is nothing at all in the world, and that there is no God but one." So an idol is not a real power in the world. It's a lot of fuss over something Paul calls nothing at all.

Right, Paul says an idol is "…nothing at all in the world…" He adds that there is no God but one. So an idol is not a real power in the world, however fancy it looks. A statue can have the best paint job in town and still be nothing at all in the world.

Moses is a giant in the Bible, but Paul doesn't name him here. He names Jesus Christ as the one Lord. Paul says all things came through Him and we exist through Him. Some names are famous, and one is Lord.

Elijah, a prophet in Israel (1 Kings 18:36), is a great name, but Paul doesn't put him here. The one Lord he names is Jesus Christ. He says all things came through Him and we exist through Him. Elijah isn't in this verse at all.

Paul says some people "…are still so accustomed to idols that they eat such food as if it were sacrificed to an idol." For them it still feels tied to the idol. Their habits haven't caught up with what others know. Paul adds that since their conscience is weak, it is defiled.

Right. Paul asks, "…will he not be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?" The one with a weak conscience sees you eating and is encouraged to eat too. That's the danger. Watching a friend can nudge somebody the wrong direction.

Paul says it straight: "…this weak brother, for whom Christ died, is destroyed by your knowledge." The knowledge itself is not the problem. It's what happens when it's used without love. Remember, love builds up (1 Corinthians 8:1). This is a heavy part.

Paul says, "…you sin against Christ." He also calls the weak brother one "…for whom Christ died…" So wounding a weak conscience is not only a squabble between two people. Paul says it is sinning against Christ.

Paul doesn't mention the law here. He says that by sinning against your brothers and wounding their weak conscience, "…you sin against Christ." He also calls the weak brother one for whom Christ died. The word he uses is Christ, not the law.
